questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

I __am not gone__ to harm this dog.
questions.solution:

• **"**Am not going**"** is grammatically incorrect in this sentence. 
 
• The correct usage is **"**Am not going**"** instead of "**am not gone**.**"**
 
• **The tense used in this sentence is Present Continuous Tense.**
 
• The Present Continuous Tense indicates that an action or condition is happening now, frequently, and may continue into the future.
 
 
• Structure of Past Perfect tense: **Subject + is/am/are + first form of the verb + ing + Object.**
 
 
• **Example:** *She is leaving for her job. *
 
 
 
 

The correct sentence is: **I am not going to harm this dog.**

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

San Francisco is more bigger/ than Boston in terms of/ population density.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **San Francisco is more bigger.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"San Francisco is more bigger"** is grammatically incorrect in this sentence. 
 
• The correct usage is **"****San Francisco is bigger****"** instead of **"San Francisco is more bigger.**"
 
• **Comparative adjectives **can be formed by adding either more or less in front of the original adjective.** **
 
 
• **Example:** *She is more interesting than him.*
 
 
 
• **Using both comparative adjectives is an error. **
 
 
• **Example:*** Elena is more smarter than Caroline. (Incorrect) *
 
 

* Elena is smarter than Caroline. (Correct)*

​The correct sentence is: **San Francisco is bigger than Boston in terms of population density.**

 The correct sentence is:** I am not willing to sign this contract with your company. **

• **"No"** is used before a noun phrase.

• The correct usage is **"Further worsen"** instead of **"Further worse."**
 
• When things go from terrible to even more terrible, we use the word **"worsen."**

• In the given sentence, the flood condition became more terrible because of the continuous heavy rainfall. That is why the word **"worsen"** should be used. 

The correct sentence is: **Continuous heavy rainfall may further worsen the flood situation.**
